title: 3187. Peaks in Array

examples.explanation: First query: We change nums[3] to 4 and nums becomes [3,1,4,4,5]. Second query: The number of peaks in the [3,1,4,4,5] is 0.
First query: nums[2] should become 4, but it is already set to 4. Second query: The number of peaks in the [4,1,4] is 0. Third query: The second 4 is a peak in the [4,1,4,2,1].

hints: Let p[i] be whether nums[i] is a peak in the original array. Namely p[i] = nums[i] > nums[i - 1] && nums[i] > nums[i + 1].
Updating nums[i], only affects p[i], p[i - 1] and p[i + 1]. We can recalculate the 3 values in constant time.
The answer for [li, ri] is p[li + 1] + p[li + 2] + … + p[ri - 1] (note that li and ri are not included).
Use some data structures (i.e. segment tree or binary indexed tree) to maintain the subarray sum efficiently.
